transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: Hi Leo. How is your numbers project going?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Quite well, actually. I've been measuring things around school, and I'm starting to see some interesting patterns.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: Patterns? Tell me more. What have you found so far?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Well, the average student spends about an hour on homework every night, which is more than I expected.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: Really? And roughly what percentage of students said that?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Around sixty percent. The amount of time surprised me too, especially on weekends.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: So the sum of all that homework time must be quite high. Did you calculate it?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Yes, I did. I also checked the probability of rain this weekend, since we're planning a school trip.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: Good thinking. Did you measure the classrooms as well?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Yes. The length of our classroom comes to nine meters, while the width is just seven.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: About three meters, although I had to estimate it from the door frame.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: What about the weight of the sports equipment?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: The football weighs around four hundred grams, though I'd like to check the shot put too.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: Great. Have you organized all your numbers?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Yes. I put them in a sequence, from smallest to largest, so the data is easier to compare.

transcript.speaker: Ms. Rivera
transcript.text: Excellent work, Leo. Your data is complete, and I'm genuinely impressed with your project.
